data.claim: Yes: a structured name {role}-{family}-{host}-{rand}, lower-case [a-z0-9-], at most 48 chars, rendered from a layered template under a [naming] section; explicit user names stay verbatim; existing names stay valid and are never renamed.
data.falsifier: A project where two offline clones share role+family+host label and draw the same 4-char suffix more than once in a thousand lanes (raise rand_length), or a harness that rejects a 48-char name.
data.mechanism: Today an agent id is free text (operator-chosen: lane3-kilo, bfix-lane1, close-bviewers; 1412 shards in .ddflow/events) or derived {host}-{tree}-{hex6} (D-B190-identity-clock). The only rule is core/agentname.AGENT_NAME [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64} (MCP) and infra.log safe_filename for the shard; there is no uniqueness check, no case-fold check, no host/family part, and swarm lanes (services/lanes/launch.py Request.agent) take whatever name the caller passes. Names collide three ways: two agents declaring one name share a shard and a lease owner; two clones with one host+tree name (B190); names differing only by case (bugfixA vs bugfixa) are two shards on Linux and one file on macOS/Windows. Best practice converges on: readable prefix plus short random suffix from a confusable-free alphabet (Kubernetes generateName appends 5 chars of bcdfghjklmnpqrstvwxz2456789; Docker uses adjective_surname with retry), DNS-label charset and length (RFC 1123: [a-z0-9-], 63), unique-by-construction when offline (random suffix, since clones cannot coordinate a counter), and a display name separate from the unique id. Git ref rules (git check-ref-format) forbid leading '-', '..', trailing '.lock', and tmux session names reject '.' and ':', so the safe generated set is [a-z0-9-]. ULID/UUIDv7 are sortable but 26/36 chars: too long for a name and the event log already orders by Lamport clock, so a 4-char suffix plus the host label is enough (4 chars of a 27-symbol alphabet is 19 bits; a clash needs the same role, family and host as well).
data.question: Should ddflow have a configurable lane/agent naming concept that is unique globally, per host and per agent family, yet readable?

data.alternatives: UUIDv7/ULID as the name (too long, unreadable; the log already orders by Lamport clock); adjective-noun names (readable but carry no host/family, need a word list to ship); a central counter (needs coordination offline clones lack); renaming existing shards (breaks lease owners and replay).
data.consequences: Generated names are longer than lane3-kilo; shorter ones remain legal when chosen. Offline clones are collision-resistant, not collision-free (19 bits of rand, plus role, family, host).
data.context: R-lane-naming-2026-11-11: ~1400 free-text shards, case-only twins (bugfixA/bugfixa), B190 clone clash, swarm lanes taking arbitrary names, remote lanes (SW-remote-*) arriving from other hosts.
data.decision: (1) A GENERATED name is {role}-{family}-{host}-{rand}: role = the human label (chosen, else derived from the item or tree), family = harness/family short name, host = short stable host label, rand = 4 chars of a vowel- and look-alike-free lower-case alphabet. Rendered from [naming].template (tokens {role} {family} {host} {rand} {seq}); charset [a-z0-9-], no leading/trailing or doubled '-', max 48 chars ([naming].max_length, hard cap 63), truncation cuts role first and never host or rand; uniqueness compared case-folded. (2) Scopes are met by construction: global (across hosts and offline clones) requires {rand}, or {seq} with {host}; host requires {seq} or {rand}; family requires {family} or {rand}; [naming].scope (default global) makes a template lacking its requirement invalid. (3) [naming].on_collision = suffix (default: a generated name that is taken re-rolls {rand}/{seq}) | refuse; the SAME owner resuming reuses its name (stable across resume, restart, re-claim). (4) A name the user or harness declares (--agent, DDFLOW_AGENT, as_agent, [agent].id) is used verbatim and never rewritten (D-user-highest-precedence-2026-11-06); it keeps today's [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64} rule; a clash with another owner is a visible warning, never a rename. (5) Existing names (lane3-kilo, bfix-lane1, [REDACTED:hostname]-x-7267fe) stay valid; no migration, no alias needed; recorded shards and lease owners are never renamed. (6) display name = the {role} part when the name matches the template, else the whole name; derived, not stored. (7) host label is machine-local: [naming].host_label lives in .ddflow/local, empty derives the lower-cased short hostname; no hostname in committed config. (8) Derived from the event log and shard directory (taken names = shards + lease holders), strict fold, no new stored state; surfaced on CLI and MCP through existing families (ddflow lanes, identify action), no new MCP tool. Defaults accepted for the model; OPEN for the operator: whether the default family part should be on by default for human-chosen roles (recommended yes), and whether on_collision default should be refuse for CI hosts.
data.title: Lane and agent names: configurable structured template, unique by construction, existing names untouched

chunk_findings.detail: `generate` fills `{seq}` with the local retry index (`attempt`, always starting at 1), but `template_problem` treats `{seq}` plus `{host}` as uniqueness across hosts and clones. Two calls with the same host label and a `taken` set that does not already contain the peer (two clones, or two processes before either name is logged) both render the same name, e.g. template `{host}-{seq}`, host `build`, `taken=()` → both return `build-1`. That is a collision the scope check claims cannot happen.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/naming.py:168

chunk_findings.detail: Global scope also treats the `{host}` token as a unique machine id, but `render` runs it through `clean(..., host_length)`, which lowercases, turns every non-alphanumeric run into `-`, and cuts to `host_length`. Distinct hosts therefore become one label: `web_1` and `web-1` both become `web-1`, and with `host_length=3` both `web-01` and `web-02` become `web`. Template `{host}-{seq}` then yields `web-1-1` or `web-1` on both machines, so the structural guarantee is false whenever the other machine’s name is absent from `taken`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/naming.py:124

chunk_findings.detail: `generate` returns a resumed name before the case-folded `taken` check. Given `current="abc-12"` and `taken=["ABC-12"]` (a different spelling, so not "this agent's own row"), `name_problem` accepts `current` and the function returns `Resolved("abc-12", "resumed")` with an empty note. On macOS/Windows those two strings are one shard file; `declared` would at least note the twin, and the module header says every generated name is compared case-folded with every taken name.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/naming.py:165

chunk_findings.detail: Template rejection runs before the resume short-circuit, so a restart does not "change nothing". Given a valid `current="worker-ab12"` and a template that `template_problem` rejects (the comment says `{rand}` is required, so `template="{role}"`), `generate` raises `NameRefused` instead of `Resolved("worker-ab12", "resumed")`. The docstring says a valid current name is kept and the template is used only otherwise.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/naming.py:163

chunk_findings.detail: If `[naming].max_tries` is 0 (or negative), `range(1, n.max_tries + 1)` is empty, `name` is never assigned, and the failure path raises `UnboundLocalError` rather than `NameRefused`. Input: any otherwise valid `Config` with `max_tries=0`, `taken=()`, `current=""`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/naming.py:186

chunk_findings.detail: `template_problem` treats the `{family}` token as enough for `scope == "family"`, but `render`/`clean` map distinct families onto one label (`"A_B"` and `"a-b"` both become `"a-b"`). Offline clones (empty `taken`, the case this check exists for) with a fixed `draw` therefore both get the same name, e.g. `a-b-x`, so the template does not actually separate those families.
